instructions: Preheat the oven to 275°F (135°C). Line a large roasting pan or rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil.
If the ribs still have a thin membrane on the back, remove it. Season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Place the ribs meaty-side down in the pan and cover tightly with foil — the ribs must be well sealed to keep from drying out.

Bake 2 1/2 to 3 1/2 hours, checking after 2 hours. The ribs are done when a sharp knife meets little resistance and the meat pulls easily from the bone; if still tough, keep baking (your oven may run cool, or raise it to 300°F).
Meanwhile, make the sauce: heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat, add the onion, and cook 5–8 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in the cumin and cook 30 seconds, then add the ketchup, chili sauce, brown sugar, and vinegar. Stir, season with salt, and cook 2 minutes.
Remove the ribs from the oven and discard the foil. Brush both sides generously with the sauce.
Move an oven rack near the top and broil on high 3–4 minutes, until the sauce caramelizes — watch closely so it doesn't burn.
kosher_review_notes: Recipe calls for baby back pork ribs, which are not kosher.
notes: NOT KOSHER as written — this recipe uses baby back pork ribs and is kept exactly as written, with no substitutions. Flagged for kosher review.

tips.text: Baking with the meatiest side facing down lets the rendered fat and juices drip down and baste the meat — the source's trick for extra-moist ribs.
tips.title: Meaty-side down

tips.text: Peeling the thin membrane off the back of the rack is the difference between fall-off-the-bone and chewy.
tips.title: Don't skip the membrane

title: Avi's Sweet and Spicy Oven-Baked Ribs
